Implementation Plan — Add runner to the history of a task\n\nTask ID: `e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146`\nWorking directory: `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146`\nSource decision: `docs/tasks/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146/idea-20261102-112913.md`\nSurvey (authoritative): `docs/tasks/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146/SURVEY.md`\n\nThis document is the plan only. No code changes are made by this stage.\n\n---\n\n## 0. Survey decisions applied (authoritative over raw wording)\n\n| Survey question | Selected answer | Implementation consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Q1 — what is a \"runner\" | A machine or computer that does the task | Only remote Runner dispatches are attributed. Backend-embedded stage runs have no runner and remain blank. Use the Runner's canonical `runnerId` (the survey note \"Use the runner label\" resolves to the operator-facing Runner id/label, never a person). |\n| Q2 — what to save about the runner | Date/time of run, Runner name/ID, pass/fail, duration | These are exactly the four fields already present on a timeline/audit-history row: `timestamp`, `runnerId`, `status`, `duration`. No new time/duration bookkeeping is required; we are adding one column (`runnerId`) to rows that already exist. |\n| Q3 — how to spot struggling | Just save the data for now, decide later | v1 persists data only. No warning flags, alerts, reports, or intervention thresholds ship in this change. They are a named follow-up that consumes the data. |\n| Q4 — what counts as struggling | All suggested (more failures, longer duration, more retries, stuck on one task type) | Document those signals for the follow-up, but do not implement detection. The persisted fields (`status`, `duration`, `infraRetryCount`/`autoIterationCount`, `task.workflowId`/`stage`) are sufficient to compute them later. |\n| Q5 — old history | Only new tasks going forward | No migration or backfill. Every row already persisted without `runnerId` stays runner-less; frontends and readers treat absence as \"unknown / not applicable\", never as a failure. |\n\n---\n\n## 1. Goals and non-goals\n\n### Goals\n\n1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n\n### Non-goals\n\n1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \"struggling runners\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\n2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\n3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\n4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\n\n---\n\n## 2. \"Make change easy, then make the change\"\n\nPer the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\n\n### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\n\n1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\n   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\n   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \"not Runner-attributed\";\n   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\n2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\n3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\n4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\n\n### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\n\n1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\n   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\n   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\n   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\n2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\n3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\n4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \"run attribution\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\n\n_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\n\n### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\n\nWire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\n\n### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\n\n1. Add `runnerId` to the in-memory audit entries that already narrate Runner work (`applyRunnerReport`'s `task.history.push`, `applyIntegrationReport`, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`), in addition to the existing `via Runner …` prose. Persist as before; no markdown format change.\n2. Ensure `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so terminal and failure rows attribute it (Phase E2 already stamps it on dispatch; this phase verifies the value flows through `completeTask` and `handleStageFailure`/`handleTransientFailure`'s existing spreads).\n3. Re-run persistence round-trip tests (§6.3).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Data model and persistence\n\n### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\n\n```\n{\n  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\n  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\n}\n```\n\n- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\n- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\n\n### 3.2 Report metadata\n\n`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName, modelRef, targetIndex }` additionally pass `runnerId`.\n\n### 3.3 Audit history entries\n\n[144 more lines in file. No code changes are made by this stage.\n\n---\n\n## 0. Survey decisions applied (authoritative over raw wording)\n\n| Survey question | Selected answer | Implementation consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Q1 — what is a \"runner\" | A machine or computer that does the task | Only remote Runner dispatches are attributed. Backend-embedded stage runs have no runner and remain blank. Use the Runner's canonical `runnerId` (the survey note \"Use the runner label\" resolves to the operator-facing Runner id/label, never a person). |\n| Q2 — what to save about the runner | Date/time of run, Runner name/ID, pass/fail, duration | These are exactly the four fields already present on a timeline/audit-history row: `timestamp`, `runnerId`, `status`, `duration`. No new time/duration bookkeeping is required; we are adding one column (`runnerId`) to rows that already exist. |\n| Q3 — how to spot struggling | Just save the data for now, decide later | v1 persists data only. No warning flags, alerts, reports, or intervention thresholds ship in this change. They are a named follow-up that consumes the data. |\n| Q4 — what counts as struggling | All suggested (more failures, longer duration, more retries, stuck on one task type) | Document those signals for the follow-up, but do not implement detection. The persisted fields (`status`, `duration`, `infraRetryCount`/`autoIterationCount`, `task.workflowId`/`stage`) are sufficient to compute them later. |\n| Q5 — old history | Only new tasks going forward | No migration or backfill. Every row already persisted without `runnerId` stays runner-less; frontends and readers treat absence as \"unknown / not applicable\", never as a failure. |\n\n---\n\n## 1. Goals and non-goals\n\n### Goals\n\n1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n\n### Non-goals\n\n1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \"struggling runners\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\n2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\n3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\n4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\n\n---\n\n## 2. \"Make change easy, then make the change\"\n\nPer the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\n\n### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\n\n1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\n   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\n   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \"not Runner-attributed\";\n   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\n2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\n3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\n4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\n\n### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\n\n1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\n   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\n   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\n   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\n2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\n3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\n4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \"run attribution\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\n\n_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\n\n### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\n\nWire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\n\n### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\n\n1. Add `runnerId` to the in-memory audit entries that already narrate Runner work (`applyRunnerReport`'s `task.history.push`, `applyIntegrationReport`, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`), in addition to the existing `via Runner …` prose. Persist as before; no markdown format change.\n2. Ensure `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so terminal and failure rows attribute it (Phase E2 already stamps it on dispatch; this phase verifies the value flows through `completeTask` and `handleStageFailure`/`handleTransientFailure`'s existing spreads).\n3. Re-run persistence round-trip tests (§6.3).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Data model and persistence\n\n### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\n\n```\n{\n  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\n  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\n}\n```\n\n- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\n- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\n\n### 3.2 Report metadata\n\n`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName, modelRef, targetIndex }` additionally pass `runnerId`.\n\n### 3.3 Audit history entries\n\n[144 more lines in file. Standards.md`.\n1|# Values\n2|\n3|## User understandable over technical language\n4|\n5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible\n6|\n7|### Principles\n8|\n9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive\n10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”\n11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)\n12|- File structure should reflect the call stack\n13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english\n14|- Include why things are done not just what is done\n15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)\n16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS\n17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality\n18|  \n19|  \n20|\n21|## Functional over Object oreintated\n22|\n23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).\n24|\n25|### Principles\n26|\n27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible\n28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that\n29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects\n30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.\n31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something\n32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.\n33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility\n34|\n35|\n36|## Co-location over abstraction\n37|\n38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.\n39|\n40|### Principles\n41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file\n42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`\n43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.\n44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders\n45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.\n46|- Don’t fear repetition of code\n47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.\n48|- Use folders as a tool for organising\n49|\n50|## Tested over trusted \n51|\n52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. \n53|\n54|### Principles\n55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function\n56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe\n57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately\n58|- Tests must be consistent\n59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app\n60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle\n61|\n62|\n63|## Fast iteration over long planning\n64|\n65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.\n66|\n67|### Principles\n68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed\n69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.\n70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.\n71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon\n72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small\n73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.\n74|\n75|\n76|\n77|# Inspirations\n78|My principles here are inspired by:\n79|\n80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)\n81|- Life isn’t binary (book)\n82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)\n83|\n84|\n85|# Examples\n86|\n87|## Intent Driven descriptions\n88|\n89|### Bad Example\n90|\n91|```js\n92|\n93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {\n94|\n95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}\n96|\n97|    users.push(user)\n98|  \n99|}\n100|\n101|const list = []\n102|\n103|userFactory(\"Frank\",32,list)\n104|\n105|\n106|```\n107|\n108|## Good example\n109|\n110|```js\n111|\n112|/**\n113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear\n114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year\n115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  \n116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4\n117|*/\n118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})\n130|\n131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: Survey decisions applied (authoritative over raw wording)\n13|\n14|| Survey question | Selected answer | Implementation consequence |\n15||---|---|---|\n16|| Q1 — what is a \"runner\" | A machine or computer that does the task | Only remote Runner dispatches are attributed. No warning flags, alerts, reports, or intervention thresholds ship in this change. They are a named follow-up that consumes the data. |\n19|| Q4 — what counts as struggling | All suggested (more failures, longer duration, more retries, stuck on one task type) | Document those signals for the follow-up, but do not implement detection. The persisted fields (`status`, `duration`, `infraRetryCount`/`autoIterationCount`, `task.workflowId`/`stage`) are sufficient to compute them later. |\n20|| Q5 — old history | Only new tasks going forward | No migration or backfill. Every row already persisted without `runnerId` stays runner-less; frontends and readers treat absence as \"unknown / not applicable\", never as a failure. |\n21|\n22|---\n23|\n24|## 1. Goals and non-goals\n25|\n26|### Goals\n27|\n28|1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n29|2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n30|3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n31|4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n32|5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n33|6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n34|\n35|### Non-goals\n36|\n37|1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \"struggling runners\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\n38|2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\n39|3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\n40|4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\n41|\n42|---\n43|\n44|## 2. \"Make change easy, then make the change\"\n45|\n46|Per the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\n47|\n48|### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\n49|\n50|1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\n51|   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\n52|   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \"not Runner-attributed\";\n53|   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\n54|2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\n55|3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\n56|4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\n57|\n58|### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\n59|\n60|1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\n61|   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\n62|   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\n63|   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\n64|2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\n65|3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\n66|4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \"run attribution\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\n67|\n68|_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\n69|\n70|### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\n71|\n72|Wire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\n73|\n74|### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\n75|\n76|1. Add `runnerId` to the in-memory audit entries that already narrate Runner work (`applyRunnerReport`'s `task.history.push`, `applyIntegrationReport`, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`), in addition to the existing `via Runner …` prose. Persist as before; no markdown format change.\n77|2. Ensure `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so terminal and failure rows attribute it (Phase E2 already stamps it on dispatch; this phase verifies the value flows through `completeTask` and `handleStageFailure`/`handleTransientFailure`'s existing spreads).\n78|3. Re-run persistence round-trip tests (§6.3).\n79|\n80|---\n81|\n82|## 3. Data model and persistence\n83|\n84|### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\n85|\n86|```\n87|{\n88|  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\n89|  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\n90|}\n91|```\n92|\n93|- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\n94|- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\n95|\n96|### 3.2 Report metadata\n97|\n98|`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName, modelRef, targetIndex }` additionally pass `runnerId`.\n99|\n100|### 3.3 Audit history entries\n101|\n102|`task.history[i]` becomes `{ timestamp, action, runnerId? }`. Confirm no runner is invented. |\n130|| `api/flow/stageTransitions.js` | `completeTask` → `runAttribution` uses `task.currentRunAttribution` | No code change if Phase 2 already carries `runnerId` through dispatch; verify via tests. |\n131|| `api/flow/executionLedger.js` | `recordProgress` `task.history.push` | Add `runnerId` to the pushed audit entry. |\n132|| `api/work/taskPersistence.js` | `reportMetadata` projection | Add `runnerId` to the destruction map. |\n133|\n134|### 4.2 Persistent markdown / parsing\n135|\n136|- No change to the `# Timeline` rendered text (runner travels in `timelineMetadata` JSON frontmatter, which already overlays parsed rows).\n137|- `saveTaskMarkdown` already JSON-stringifies `timelineMetadata` containing the full timeline objects, so once rows include `runnerId` it is persisted.\n138|- `parseTaskMarkdown` already restores `timeline` from `parseStoredRecords(data.timelineMetadata)` when non-empty. Confirm (yes, line `if (persistedTimeline.length > 0) timeline = persistedTimeline;`).\n139|- `parseStoredRecords` must preserve unknown keys; verify and cover with a test.\n140|\n141|### 4.3 Frontend (optional; can defer without breaking data capture)\n142|\n143|- `frontend/src/components/tasks/RunAttributionBadge.jsx::formatRunAttribution`: optionally append `runnerId` as `via runner <id>` in the badge/expansion. Stage testing plan\n159|\n160|### Unit\n161|\n162|1. `api/flow/runAttribution.test.js` (add/extend):\n163|   - `buildTimelineAttribution({ runnerId: \"runner-alpha\" })` returns `{ runnerId: \"runner-alpha\" }` even with no harness/model.\n164|   - `buildTimelineAttribution({})` still returns `null`.\n165|   - `stampArrivalRowAttribution(task, label, { runnerId })` stamps `runnerId` on the matching arrival row.\n166|2. `api/work/taskPersistence.test.js` (add cases):\n167|   - `saveTaskMarkdown` → `parseTaskMarkdown` round-trips `runnerId` on timeline rows and report entries.\n168|   - A row/report without `runnerId` parses and renders identically (backward compatibility).\n169|3. `api/flow/execution/applyRunnerReport.test.js` (extend):\n170|   - On pass, the last timeline/audit entry contains `runnerId` equal to `outcome.runnerId`.\n171|   - On failure, `routeStageError` receives `runOutcome.runnerId` and the resulting Failed row persists it.\n172|   - Report metadata includes `runnerId`.\n173|4. `api/flow/routing/*` tests for `handleStageFailure` / `handleTransientFailure`:\n174|   - `runnerId` passed via opts appears on the Failed/Retrying timeline row and `saveStageReport` call.\n175|5. `runnerRoutes` dispatch/claim tests:\n176|   - A dispatch assignment stamps `currentRunAttribution.runnerId` (and arrival row `runnerId`) for the claiming runner.\n177|6. Audit ledger test:\n178|   - `executionLedger.recordProgress` pushes an audit entry that carries structured `runnerId`.\n179|\n180|### Integration\n181|\n182|1. Dispatch a task to a test Runner, complete it, reload from disk, assert the timeline row and report metadata contain the Runner id.\n183|2. Force a failure on the runner path, reload, assert the Failed row and failure report contain the Runner id.\n184|3. Run `npm run test:unit` with zero regressions.\n185|\n186|### Verification gate\n187|\n188|- `npm run test:unit` is the primary gate (per task verification guidance).\n189|- No long-lived server; use existing Vitest/runner mocks.\n190|- Add a changelog note if the project's test runner list requires new test files (`scripts/run-tests.mjs` pinned list) — confirm any added test file is registered there.\n191|\n192|---\n193|\n194|## 6. Edge cases / compatibility\n195|\n196|1. **Embedded runs**: no `runnerId` is stamped or persisted. Rows without it are indistinguishable from pre-feature history, which is intended (survey Q5).\n197|2. **Renamed/removed Runners**: rows hard-code `runnerId` strings. Readers must not join against the live registry to interpret history. This matches the precedent for `aliasName` (renaming aliases orphans prior history).\n198|3. **Terminal `Completed` row**: emitted in `completeTask` only when `currentRunAttribution` matches the current stage. For a Runner that ran the final stage, `runnerId` flows through; otherwise absent.\n199|4. **Retries**: `handleTransientFailure` records two rows (retrying + terminal/exhausted); both must carry the same `runnerId` when the failing run was Runner-attributed.\n200|5. **Report metadata projection**: adding `runnerId` to the projection must not hide it when reports are saved; ensure `saveStageReport` accepts and `TaskPersistence.saveTaskMarkdown` serializes it. Missing field on a report serializes as `undefined` dropped by JSON — consistent with existing optional fields.\n201|6. **Markdown parser safety**: if a timeline row line lacks the runner (always, since runner is in frontmatter JSON), no parser change is needed. If we optionally render runner in `# Timeline` text, that would require parser care; avoid in v1.\n202|7. **Concurrency**: no lock required; rows are appended single-writer under the owning task.\n203|\n204|---\n205|\n206|## 7. Optional display pass (deferred, survey Q3)\n207|\n208|If desired in the same change, a trivial presentation update without behaviour:\n209|\n210|- `RunAttributionBadge.jsx`: include `runnerId` in the tooltip (`runner: …`) and optionally render `via <runnerId>` as an additional muted segment.\n211|- `TaskDetailHistoryPane.jsx` audit events: render `runnerId` when present on an audit entry.\n212|- Frontend tests: update `RunAttributionBadge.test.jsx` expectations.\n213|\n214|This is explicitly **not required** for struggling detection, which should be computed from persisted data, not from rendered text. Deferring keeps the change minimal per \"make change easy, then make the change.\"\n215|\n216|---\n217|\n218|## 8. Risks\n219|\n220|1. **Build timeline attribution semantics change**: extending `buildTimelineAttribution` to return `runnerId`-only rows could make CI/merge rows carry runner data where they previously carried nothing. This is exactly the goal, but callers that spread `runAttribution || {}` into timeline rows must continue to filter falsy. Mitigation: only emit `runnerId` when a real Runner is authenticated.\n221|2. **Over-broad scope**: wiring every failure path in one pass risks missing a site. Mitigation: §4.1 table plus a final grep for `runOutcome`, `saveStageReport`, and `buildTimelineAttribution` to catch un-wired sites; add a regression test that greps for omitted `runnerId` where `harnessId` is passed.\n222|3. **Frontend/backend divergence**: frontend types (none today) don't need updating because data is carried in JSON metadata. Keep frontend changes to optional display only.\n223|4. **Test registration**: `scripts/run-tests.mjs` pins runner tests by filename. If new test files are added, register them or they won't run. Mitigation: prefer extending existing test files over new ones.\n224|\n225|---\n226|\n227|## 9. Acceptance criteria\n228|\n229|1. A successful Runner-run stage produces a persisted timeline row with `runnerId` equal to the Runner that ran it.\n230|2. A failed or retried Runner-run stage produces each resulting row (Failed / Retrying / exhausted) with the same `runnerId`.\n231|3. Stage reports generated on the Runner path carry `runnerId` in `reportMetadata`.\n232|4. A terminal `Completed` row for a Runner-run final stage carries `runnerId`.\n233|5. Embedded runs leave `runnerId` absent on all rows/reports; no placeholder id is invented.\n234|6. Reloads from disk preserve `runnerId` on timeline and report rows.\n235|7. Existing tests pass without modification except tests legitimately extended to cover the new field; no snapshots/regressions.\n236|8. `npm run test:unit` passes after each phase.\n237|\n238|---\n239|\n240|## 10. Rollout / \"no migration\" note\n241|\n242|This change is additive and forward-only. Tasks already on disk keep their current (runner-less) rows and reports unchanged; they simply lack `runnerId` and remain valid. Survey decisions applied (authoritative over raw wording)\n\n| Survey question | Selected answer | Implementation consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Q1 — what is a \"runner\" | A machine or computer that does the task | Only remote Runner dispatches are attributed. Backend-embedded stage runs have no runner and remain blank. No warning flags, alerts, reports, or intervention thresholds ship in this change. Goals and non-goals\n\n### Goals\n\n1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n\n### Non-goals\n\n1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \"struggling runners\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\n2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\n3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\n4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\n\n---\n\n## 2. \"Make change easy, then make the change\"\n\nPer the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\n\n### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\n\n1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\n   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\n   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \"not Runner-attributed\";\n   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\n2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\n3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\n4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\n\n### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\n\n1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\n   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\n   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\n   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\n2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\n3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\n4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \"run attribution\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\n\n_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\n\n### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\n\nWire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\n\n### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\n\n1. Add `runnerId` to the in-memory audit entries that already narrate Runner work (`applyRunnerReport`'s `task.history.push`, `applyIntegrationReport`, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`), in addition to the existing `via Runner …` prose. Persist as before; no markdown format change.\n2. Ensure `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so terminal and failure rows attribute it (Phase E2 already stamps it on dispatch; this phase verifies the value flows through `completeTask` and `handleStageFailure`/`handleTransientFailure`'s existing spreads).\n3. Re-run persistence round-trip tests (§6.3).\n\n---\n\n## 3. Data model and persistence\n\n### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\n\n```\n{\n  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\n  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\n}\n```\n\n- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\n- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\n\n### 3.2 Report metadata\n\n`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName, modelRef, targetIndex }` additionally pass `runnerId`.\n\n### 3.3 Audit history entries\n\n`task.history[i]` becomes `{ timestamp, action, runnerId? }`. Markdown rendering stays `- timestamp: action`; the structured field is retained via the existing in-memory object and best-effort rendering. Audit entries emitted by the Runner transport also include the structured field so downstream consumers need not parse the `\"Runner X stage Y: event\"` string.\n\n### 3.4 Source of truth\n\n- Dispatch allocates `runnerId` from the authenticated Runner credential (`runner.runnerId`), never from the request body. This matches the existing scope rule (R04): claim, dispatch, direct claim, and skip all use the authenticated Runner.\n- Amplify fail safety: if no Runner is authenticated (embedded path), leave `currentRunAttribution.runnerId` unset; do not invent an id.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Audit ledger test:\n   - `executionLedger.recordProgress` pushes an audit entry that carries structured `runnerId`.\n\n### Integration\n\n1. Dispatch a task to a test Runner, complete it, reload from disk, assert the timeline row and report metadata contain the Runner id.\n2. Force a failure on the runner path, reload, assert the Failed row and failure report contain the Runner id.\n3. Run `npm run test:unit` with zero regressions.\n\n### Verification gate\n\n- `npm run test:unit` is the primary gate (per task verification guidance).\n- No long-lived server; use existing Vitest/runner mocks.\n- Add a changelog note if the project's test runner list requires new test files (`scripts/run-tests.mjs` pinned list) — confirm any added test file is registered there.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Edge cases / compatibility\n\n1. **Embedded runs**: no `runnerId` is stamped or persisted. Rows without it are indistinguishable from pre-feature history, which is intended (survey Q5).\n2. **Renamed/removed Runners**: rows hard-code `runnerId` strings. Readers must not join against the live registry to interpret history. This matches the precedent for `aliasName` (renaming aliases orphans prior history).\n3. **Terminal `Completed` row**: emitted in `completeTask` only when `currentRunAttribution` matches the current stage. For a Runner that ran the final stage, `runnerId` flows through; otherwise absent.\n4. **Retries**: `handleTransientFailure` records two rows (retrying + terminal/exhausted); both must carry the same `runnerId` when the failing run was Runner-attributed.\n5. **Report metadata projection**: adding `runnerId` to the projection must not hide it when reports are saved; ensure `saveStageReport` accepts and `TaskPersistence.saveTaskMarkdown` serializes it. Missing field on a report serializes as `undefined` dropped by JSON — consistent with existing optional fields.\n6. **Markdown parser safety**: if a timeline row line lacks the runner (always, since runner is in frontmatter JSON), no parser change is needed. If we optionally render runner in `# Timeline` text, that would require parser care; avoid in v1.\n7. **Concurrency**: no lock required; rows are appended single-writer under the owning task.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Optional display pass (deferred, survey Q3)\n\nIf desired in the same change, a trivial presentation update without behaviour:\n\n- `RunAttributionBadge.jsx`: include `runnerId` in the tooltip (`runner: …`) and optionally render `via <runnerId>` as an additional muted segment.\n- `TaskDetailHistoryPane.jsx` audit events: render `runnerId` when present on an audit entry.\n- Frontend tests: update `RunAttributionBadge.test.jsx` expectations.\n\nThis is explicitly **not required** for struggling detection, which should be computed from persisted data, not from rendered text. Deferring keeps the change minimal per \"make change easy, then make the change.\"\n\n---\n\n## 8. Risks\n\n1. **Build timeline attribution semantics change**: extending `buildTimelineAttribution` to return `runnerId`-only rows could make CI/merge rows carry runner data where they previously carried nothing. This is exactly the goal, but callers that spread `runAttribution || {}` into timeline rows must continue to filter falsy. Mitigation: only emit `runnerId` when a real Runner is authenticated.\n2. **Over-broad scope**: wiring every failure path in one pass risks missing a site. Mitigation: §4.1 table plus a final grep for `runOutcome`, `saveStageReport`, and `buildTimelineAttribution` to catch un-wired sites; add a regression test that greps for omitted `runnerId` where `harnessId` is passed.\n3. **Frontend/backend divergence**: frontend types (none today) don't need updating because data is carried in JSON metadata. Keep frontend changes to optional display only.\n4. **Test registration**: `scripts/run-tests.mjs` pins runner tests by filename. If new test files are added, register them or they won't run. Mitigation: prefer extending existing test files over new ones.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance criteria\n\n1. A successful Runner-run stage produces a persisted timeline row with `runnerId` equal to the Runner that ran it.\n2. A failed or retried Runner-run stage produces each resulting row (Failed / Retrying / exhausted) with the same `runnerId`.\n3. Stage reports generated on the Runner path carry `runnerId` in `reportMetadata`.\n4. A terminal `Completed` row for a Runner-run final stage carries `runnerId`.\n5. Embedded runs leave `runnerId` absent on all rows/reports; no placeholder id is invented.\n6. Reloads from disk preserve `runnerId` on timeline and report rows.\n7. Existing tests pass without modification except tests legitimately extended to cover the new field; no snapshots/regressions.\n8. `npm run test:unit` passes after each phase.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Rollout / \"no migration\" note\n\nThis change is additive and forward-only. Tasks already on disk keep their current (runner-less) rows and reports unchanged; they simply lack `runnerId` and remain valid. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n\n### Non-goals\n\n1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \"struggling runners\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\n2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\n3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\n4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\n\n---\n\n## 2. \"Make change easy, then make the change\"\n\nPer the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\n\n### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\n\n1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\n   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\n   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \"not Runner-attributed\";\n   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\n2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\n3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\n4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\n\n### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\n\n1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\n   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\n   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\n   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\n2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\n3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\n4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \"run attribution\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\n\n_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\n\n### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\n\nWire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\n\n### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\n\n1. Data model and persistence\n\n### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\n\n```\n{\n  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\n  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\n}\n```\n\n- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\n- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\n\n### 3.2 Report metadata\n\n`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName, modelRef, targetIndex }` additionally pass `runnerId`.\n\n### 3.3 Audit history entries\n\n`task.history[i]` becomes `{ timestamp, action, runnerId? }`. Markdown rendering stays `- timestamp: action`; the structured field is retained via the existing in-memory object and best-effort rendering. Audit entries emitted by the Runner transport also include the structured field so downstream consumers need not parse the `\"Runner X stage Y: event\"` string.\n\n### 3.4 Source of truth\n\n- Dispatch allocates `runnerId` from the authenticated Runner credential (`runner.runnerId`), never from the request body. This matches the existing scope rule (R04): claim, dispatch, direct claim, and skip all use the authenticated Runner.\n- Amplify fail safety: if no Runner is authenticated (embedded path), leave `currentRunAttribution.runnerId` unset; do not invent an id.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Edge cases / compatibility\n\n1. **Embedded runs**: no `runnerId` is stamped or persisted. Rows without it are indistinguishable from pre-feature history, which is intended (survey Q5).\n2. **Renamed/removed Runners**: rows hard-code `runnerId` strings. Readers must not join against the live registry to interpret history. This matches the precedent for `aliasName` (renaming aliases orphans prior history).\n3. **Terminal `Completed` row**: emitted in `completeTask` only when `currentRunAttribution` matches the current stage. For a Runner that ran the final stage, `runnerId` flows through; otherwise absent.\n4. **Retries**: `handleTransientFailure` records two rows (retrying + terminal/exhausted); both must carry the same `runnerId` when the failing run was Runner-attributed.\n5. **Report metadata projection**: adding `runnerId` to the projection must not hide it when reports are saved; ensure `saveStageReport` accepts and `TaskPersistence.saveTaskMarkdown` serializes it. Missing field on a report serializes as `undefined` dropped by JSON — consistent with existing optional fields.\n6. **Markdown parser safety**: if a timeline row line lacks the runner (always, since runner is in frontmatter JSON), no parser change is needed. If we optionally render runner in `# Timeline` text, that would require parser care; avoid in v1.\n7. **Concurrency**: no lock required; rows are appended single-writer under the owning task.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Deferring keeps the change minimal per \"make change easy, then make the change.\"\n\n---\n\n## 8. Risks\n\n1. **Build timeline attribution semantics change**: extending `buildTimelineAttribution` to return `runnerId`-only rows could make CI/merge rows carry runner data where they previously carried nothing. This is exactly the goal, but callers that spread `runAttribution || {}` into timeline rows must continue to filter falsy. Mitigation: only emit `runnerId` when a real Runner is authenticated.\n2. **Over-broad scope**: wiring every failure path in one pass risks missing a site. Mitigation: §4.1 table plus a final grep for `runOutcome`, `saveStageReport`, and `buildTimelineAttribution` to catch un-wired sites; add a regression test that greps for omitted `runnerId` where `harnessId` is passed.\n3. **Frontend/backend divergence**: frontend types (none today) don't need updating because data is carried in JSON metadata. Keep frontend changes to optional display only.\n4. **Test registration**: `scripts/run-tests.mjs` pins runner tests by filename. If new test files are added, register them or they won't run. Mitigation: prefer extending existing test files over new ones.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance criteria\n\n1. A successful Runner-run stage produces a persisted timeline row with `runnerId` equal to the Runner that ran it.\n2. A failed or retried Runner-run stage produces each resulting row (Failed / Retrying / exhausted) with the same `runnerId`.\n3. Stage reports generated on the Runner path carry `runnerId` in `reportMetadata`.\n4. A terminal `Completed` row for a Runner-run final stage carries `runnerId`.\n5. Embedded runs leave `runnerId` absent on all rows/reports; no placeholder id is invented.\n6. Reloads from disk preserve `runnerId` on timeline and report rows.\n7. Existing tests pass without modification except tests legitimately extended to cover the new field; no snapshots/regressions.\n8. `npm run test:unit` passes after each phase.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Tasks already on disk keep their current (runner-less) rows and reports unchanged; they simply lack `runnerId` and remain valid. Goals and non-goals\n\n### Goals\n\n1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\"embedded\"`, `\"local\"`, etc.).\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\n\n### Non-goals\n\n1. Optional display pass (deferred, survey Q3)\n\nIf desired in the same change, a trivial presentation update without behaviour:\n\n- `RunAttributionBadge.jsx`: include `runnerId` in the tooltip (`runner: …`) and optionally render `via <runnerId>` as an additional muted segment.\n- `TaskDetailHistoryPane.jsx` audit events: render `runnerId` when present on an audit entry.\n- Frontend tests: update `RunAttributionBadge.test.jsx` expectations.\n\nThis is explicitly **not required** for struggling detection, which should be computed from persisted data, not from rendered text. Deferring keeps the change minimal per \"make change easy, then make the change.\"\n\n---\n\n## 8. Risks\n\n1. **Build timeline attribution semantics change**: extending `buildTimelineAttribution` to return `runnerId`-only rows could make CI/merge rows carry runner data where they previously carried nothing. This is exactly the goal, but callers that spread `runAttribution || {}` into timeline rows must continue to filter falsy. Mitigation: only emit `runnerId` when a real Runner is authenticated.\n2. **Over-broad scope**: wiring every failure path in one pass risks missing a site. Mitigation: §4.1 table plus a final grep for `runOutcome`, `saveStageReport`, and `buildTimelineAttribution` to catch un-wired sites; add a regression test that greps for omitted `runnerId` where `harnessId` is passed.\n3. **Frontend/backend divergence**: frontend types (none today) don't need updating because data is carried in JSON metadata. Keep frontend changes to optional display only.\n4. **Test registration**: `scripts/run-tests.mjs` pins runner tests by filename. If new test files are added, register them or they won't run. Mitigation: prefer extending existing test files over new ones.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Acceptance criteria\n\n1. A successful Runner-run stage produces a persisted timeline row with `runnerId` equal to the Runner that ran it.\n2. A failed or retried Runner-run stage produces each resulting row (Failed / Retrying / exhausted) with the same `runnerId`.\n3. Stage reports generated on the Runner path carry `runnerId` in `reportMetadata`.\n4. A terminal `Completed` row for a Runner-run final stage carries `runnerId`.\n5. Embedded runs leave `runnerId` absent on all rows/reports; no placeholder id is invented.\n6. Reloads from disk preserve `runnerId` on timeline and report rows.\n7. Existing tests pass without modification except tests legitimately extended to cover the new field; no snapshots/regressions.\n8. `npm run test:unit` passes after each phase.\n\n---\n\n## 10. Rollout / \"no migration\" note\n\nThis change is additive and forward-only. Tasks already on disk keep their current (runner-less) rows and reports unchanged; they simply lack `runnerId` and remain valid. Struggling-runner detection (survey Q3/Q4) will be implemented as a separate follow-up consumer of these persisted fields and can choose its own thresholds without further schema work.\n\nKAINBAIN_VERDICT: PASS","durationMs":44}},{"id":10,"ts":"2026-11-03T21:13:13.572Z","feed":"tools","feeds":["tools"],"kind":"tool","turn":2,"text":"[RESULT] On branch kb/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146 Your branch is up to date with 'origin/kb/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146'. Implementation Plan — Add runner to the history of a task\\n\\nTask ID: `e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146`\\nWorking directory: `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/kb-e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146`\\nSource decision: `docs/tasks/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146/idea-20261102-112913.md`\\nSurvey (authoritative): `docs/tasks/e60de7fa-113f-414c-9192-0ac11973b146/SURVEY.md`\\n\\nThis document is the plan only. No code changes are made by this stage.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 0. Survey decisions applied (authoritative over raw wording)\\n\\n| Survey question | Selected answer | Implementation consequence |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Q1 — what is a \\\"runner\\\" | A machine or computer that does the task | Only remote Runner dispatches are attributed. Backend-embedded stage runs have no runner and remain blank. Use the Runner's canonical `runnerId` (the survey note \\\"Use the runner label\\\" resolves to the operator-facing Runner id/label, never a person). |\\n| Q2 — what to save about the runner | Date/time of run, Runner name/ID, pass/fail, duration | These are exactly the four fields already present on a timeline/audit-history row: `timestamp`, `runnerId`, `status`, `duration`. No new time/duration bookkeeping is required; we are adding one column (`runnerId`) to rows that already exist. |\\n| Q3 — how to spot struggling | Just save the data for now, decide later | v1 persists data only. No warning flags, alerts, reports, or intervention thresholds ship in this change. They are a named follow-up that consumes the data. |\\n| Q4 — what counts as struggling | All suggested (more failures, longer duration, more retries, stuck on one task type) | Document those signals for the follow-up, but do not implement detection. The persisted fields (`status`, `duration`, `infraRetryCount`/`autoIterationCount`, `task.workflowId`/`stage`) are sufficient to compute them later. |\\n| Q5 — old history | Only new tasks going forward | No migration or backfill. Every row already persisted without `runnerId` stays runner-less; frontends and readers treat absence as \\\"unknown / not applicable\\\", never as a failure. |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 1. Goals and non-goals\\n\\n### Goals\\n\\n1. Every stage-transition row (task history timeline) recorded for a Runner-run stage persists `runnerId` in its structured fields, for both successful and failed runs and every retry/recovering outcome.\\n2. Every stage report's persisted metadata (`reportMetadata`) carries `runnerId` for the Runner that ran it.\\n3. The persisted `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so the terminal `Completed` row and any failure close-out row attribute the Runner that ran the stage.\\n4. Embedded (backend) runs continue to attribute no Runner, so `runnerId` stays absent rather than becoming a placeholder (`\\\"embedded\\\"`, `\\\"local\\\"`, etc.).\\n5. Build and persistence remain backward-compatible: rows and reports without `runnerId` parse and render exactly as before (no migration).\\n6. Data survives reload/restart because it travels through the existing structured JSON frontmatter (`timelineMetadata`, `reportMetadata`), not through the rendered Markdown sections.\\n\\n### Non-goals\\n\\n1. No UI intervention workflow, alerting, or dashboard for \\\"struggling runners\\\" (survey Q3/Q4): this change is capture only.\\n2. No changes to dispatch selection, runner matching, or operator config.\\n3. No user-facing redesign beyond making the saved id available to the existing attribution surface (optional display pass, §7). If a display update is deferred, the data is still queryable from task files/API.\\n4. No historical migration/backfill of tasks that ran before the change (survey Q5).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 2. \\\"Make change easy, then make the change\\\"\\n\\nPer the project standard, land small preparatory refactors first so the real change is mechanical, and run `npm run test:unit` after Phase E.\\n\\n### Phase E0 — Easy (research + contract decisions, no behaviour change)\\n\\n1. **Pin the public contract for the new field.** Decide and document:\\n   - field name `runnerId` (matches the casing already used by `task.currentRunAttribution`, Runner registry, and `PerRunnerTasksWidget`);\\n   - it is optional on every row/report and absent means \\\"not Runner-attributed\\\";\\n   - it is additive only — never overwrite or migration-heal existing rows.\\n2. **Confirm parsing pass-through.** Verify `parseStoredRecords` keeps unknown keys (it does today for `aliasName`, `modelRef`, `targetIndex` added earlier); add one characterization test if missing.\\n3. **Identify every write site** before touching code (list in §4.1). Include `completeTask`, `advanceStage`/`moveToStage` arrival rows, `handleStageFailure`, `handleTransientFailure`, `applyRunnerReport`, `applyIntegrationReport`, dispatch stamping, claim path, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`.\\n4. **Agree frontend scope.** Confirm we are not required to render the new field in v1 (data capture first). The optional display item is §7, not a goal.\\n\\n### Phase E1 — Refactor to make the change mechanical (no behaviour change)\\n\\n1. Extend `buildTimelineAttribution` (`api/flow/runAttribution.js`) to accept and preserve `runnerId`:\\n   - clean it the same way as harness/model strings (`typeof string`, trim, drop blank);\\n   - return it even when `harnessId` and `modelRef` are absent, because CI/merge/integration rows are stage-closing rows where the only attribution may be the Runner itself;\\n   - keep the null contract for *both* harness/model *and* runner all absent.\\n2. Extend `stampArrivalRowAttribution` / `stampDispatchRunAttribution` plumbing to thread the new value (surfaces, does not change behaviour yet).\\n3. Add `runnerId` to the `saveTaskMarkdown` report metadata projection (`api/work/taskPersistence.js`) so it is persisted on every write once a report carries it (projection is harmless until writes include it).\\n4. Add `runnerId` to the documented \\\"run attribution\\\" vocabulary in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` and `docs/KB Architecture.md` as a sibling field to `harnessId`/`modelRef`.\\n\\n_Phase E1 must pass existing tests (`npm run test:unit`) before proceeding. It is behaviourally inert because no write site supplies `runnerId` yet._\\n\\n### Phase E2 — The change (add runner to history)\\n\\nWire `runnerId` through every stage write site listed in §4.1 so a Runner-attributed run records the Runner on its timeline row and report. Each is a one-line attribution addition, exactly analogous to the existing `harnessId`/`modelRef`/`aliasName`/`targetIndex` fields.\\n\\n### Phase E3 — Audit entries, persistence, and close-out\\n\\n1. Add `runnerId` to the in-memory audit entries that already narrate Runner work (`applyRunnerReport`'s `task.history.push`, `applyIntegrationReport`, and `executionLedger.recordProgress`), in addition to the existing `via Runner …` prose. Persist as before; no markdown format change.\\n2. Ensure `task.currentRunAttribution` carries `runnerId` so terminal and failure rows attribute it (Phase E2 already stamps it on dispatch; this phase verifies the value flows through `completeTask` and `handleStageFailure`/`handleTransientFailure`'s existing spreads).\\n3. Re-run persistence round-trip tests (§6.3).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 3. Data model and persistence\\n\\n### 3.1 Timeline row fields (additive)\\n\\n```\\n{\\n  stage, status, duration, timestamp, diff/boundary fields,\\n  harnessId?, modelRef?, aliasName?, targetIndex?, runnerId?  // NEW\\n}\\n```\\n\\n- `runnerId` is optional and absent (never `null`-worded) when the stage ran embedded or is pre-feature history.\\n- It is a plain string copied from the authenticated Runner record (`runner.runnerId`), never resolved through an alias or registry lookup at read time. This keeps the row interpretable after a Runner is renamed/removed.\\n\\n### 3.2 Report metadata\\n\\n`reportMetadata` projection in `saveTaskMarkdown` adds `runnerId` to its field list. Report files are JSON entries in frontmatter, so `parseStoredRecords` already keeps it. `saveStageReport` call sites that currently pass `{ harnessId, failureKind, aliasName,
